package_info.package_name: OKX Binance & Huobi VIP fee comparision.xls / CryptoDashboardV2
package_info.package_manager: malicious Excel macro + MSI installer (Windows ecosystem)
package_info.why_malicious: The package chain is designed to deliver and execute a multi-stage malware attack: a weaponized Excel file with obfuscated macros drops a secondary payload, which downloads and executes further malware via DLL side-loading and backdoor installation, ultimately enabling remote access, data exfiltration, and C2 communication.

execution_context.trigger: user opens Excel and enables macros
execution_context.file_location: OKX Binance & Huobi VIP fee comparision.xls (VBA macro)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Malicious macro abuses a VBA UserForm to obfuscate code, extracts a base64-encoded Excel sheet, writes it to C:\ProgramData\Microsoft Media\VSDB688.tmp, and executes it in invisible mode.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Upon macro execution, the code uses obfuscated VBA to extract and decode a hidden Excel sheet, writes it as VSDB688.tmp to a hidden directory, and executes it invisibly, enabling further payload delivery.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Macros that write and execute hidden files in system directories are a common malware tactic, especially when obfuscated.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal Excel macros should not drop or execute hidden files, nor use obfuscation to hide their actions.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some enterprise macros may automate file exports, but not with this level of obfuscation or hidden execution.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: VSDB688.tmp downloads a PNG file from hxxps://od[.]lk/d/d021d412be456a6f78a0052a1f0e3557dcfa14bf25f9d0f1d0d2d7dcdac86c73/Background.png, extracts three executables: logagent.exe (legit), wsock32.dll (malicious), and an XOR-encoded backdoor.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: After being executed, the code downloads a PNG file from a remote server, extracts embedded executables (including a malicious DLL and backdoor), and writes them to disk for further execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Downloading files disguised as images and extracting executables is a known malware delivery technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software does not download executables embedded in image files.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some installers may download dependencies, but not in this obfuscated, multi-stage manner.
key_indicators: Extracts and writes executables from image

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: logagent.exe is used to sideload the malicious wsock32.dll, which acts as a DLL proxy to the legitimate wsock32.dll. The malicious DLL loads and decrypts the XOR-encoded backdoor.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When logagent.exe is run, it loads wsock32.dll from the same directory (DLL side-loading), which then decrypts and loads the backdoor, enabling remote access.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: DLL side-loading is a common malware persistence and evasion technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate DLLs should not decrypt and load hidden backdoors.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: DLL proxying is used in some legitimate software for compatibility, but not for loading hidden payloads.
key_indicators: Malicious DLL acts as proxy but loads backdoor

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: XOR-encoded backdoor, once decrypted, establishes C2 communication with strainservice.com or 198.54.115.248, encodes data, and enables remote access and exfiltration.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the backdoor connects to a remote C2 server over HTTP/HTTPS, encodes data, and allows the attacker to remotely access and exfiltrate information from the infected system.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Unsolicited outbound connections to C2 infrastructure and data encoding are classic backdoor behaviors.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software should not establish covert C2 channels or exfiltrate data.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Remote management tools, but these are not hidden or encoded in this way.
key_indicators: C2 communication to known malicious domain/IP

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: MSI package installs a fake CryptoDashboardV2 app, drops Duser.dll (malicious), which is then side-loaded by a legitimate executable (TPLink.exe), loading an implant.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Upon installation, the MSI drops a malicious DLL (Duser.dll) and arranges for it to be loaded by a legitimate executable, which then loads an implant for persistence and further malicious activity.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Fake installers that drop malicious DLLs for side-loading are a hallmark of supply chain and targeted attacks.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate installers do not drop DLLs designed for side-loading by unrelated executables.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some software uses DLLs for plugins, but not in this deceptive manner.
key_indicators: DLL acts as proxy but loads implant
Installer masquerades as legitimate crypto app

attack_chain.action: User receives and opens weaponized Excel file, enabling macros.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious macro execution and payload drop

attack_chain.action: Macro extracts and executes hidden payload (VSDB688.tmp), which downloads further malware.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malware components downloaded and written to disk

attack_chain.action: Downloaded logagent.exe is executed, side-loading malicious wsock32.dll, which decrypts and loads the backdoor.
Backdoor establishes C2 communication, enabling remote access and data exfiltration.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains control and can exfiltrate data

attack_chain.action: User may also execute a fake MSI installer (CryptoDashboardV2), which drops and side-loads another malicious DLL (Duser.dll) for persistence.

behavioral_signatures: Office applications (Excel, Word) creating files in uncommon or hidden directories (e.g., C:\ProgramData\Microsoft Media\)
Office apps downloading files with uncommon extensions or from suspicious domains
DLL side-loading by legitimate executables (logagent.exe, TPLink.exe) with malicious DLLs (wsock32.dll, Duser.dll)
Executables or DLLs making outbound connections to known C2 domains/IPs
Obfuscated VBA macros using UserForms and hidden payloads
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for Office applications creating or executing files in uncommon or hidden directories, especially those matching known IOCs. Detect DLL side-loading by monitoring legitimate executables (logagent.exe, TPLink.exe) loading DLLs from user-writable or non-standard locations. Alert on outbound connections to known C2 domains/IPs or on encoded/obfuscated network traffic from suspicious processes. Use EDR to flag obfuscated VBA macros, especially those using UserForms or writing hidden files. Correlate file creation, process execution, and network activity for multi-stage attacks.
